name: Sirpreet Dhillon
headline: AI engineer who ships production LLM, data, and edge-ML systems end to end.
intro: PLACEHOLDER — I design, build, and deploy AI-powered software for teams that need it to work in the real world: from RAG assistants and data pipelines to ML running on satellites.
availability: Open to AI / forward deployed engineer roles and select freelance projects
bio: PLACEHOLDER — I'm a software and AI engineer with a BASc in Computer Engineering from Simon Fraser University. Since 2019 I've worked independently with companies to turn messy problems into reliable systems: LLM assistants grounded in their own data, analytics pipelines, and cloud architectures that don't fall over.

PLACEHOLDER — My background spans hardware and software: bio-amplifier and fNIRS work in an SFU engineering lab, medical imaging pipelines in a cancer research lab, and test automation at Ford. Today I'm focused on running ML directly on edge TPUs aboard satellites.

currentWork.title: Onboard SAR processing on edge TPUs
currentWork.summary: Satellites spend most of their downlink budget sending raw synthetic-aperture radar data to the ground. I'm building a pipeline that turns the raw radar signal into ML answers onboard, so the satellite sends back the result, not the raw data.
points: PLACEHOLDER — Raw SAR signal → focused image formation tuned for constrained hardware
PLACEHOLDER — Quantized models compiled for edge TPUs, running inference in orbit
PLACEHOLDER — Downlink shrinks from gigabytes of raw data to compact detections and metadata
